question: Why is the blue subpixel usually the largest on an OLED screen?
answer: Because blue emitters age fastest. Red and green use phosphorescent molecules that turn nearly every injected charge into light, but a long-lived phosphorescent blue has long proved elusive, so blue uses less efficient ones. A bigger blue area runs at lower current density, which slows its ageing and stops whites drifting yellow.
move: The weakest part sets the design; everything else is sized around it.
reference: Liao, Klubek & Tang, Full-color organic display having improved blue emission, US Patent 7,030,554, Eastman Kodak, 2006
